newsitem.title: FRANCE: SOCCER-PSG END TOUGH SEASON WITH EUROPEAN CUP BERTH.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-PSG END TOUGH SEASON WITH EUROPEAN CUP BERTH.

text.p: Ambitious Paris St Germain suffered this season but nevertheless managed to snatch a place in the European Cup.
A dramatic late goal by midfielder Vincent Guerin gave the Paris club a 2-1 win over Strasbourg in their final league match on Saturday.
The victory allowed PSG to finish second, three points ahead of Nantes who were beaten 2-1 by champions Monaco with Brazilian striker Anderson scoring the winner in injury time.
The 38,000 fans packing Parc des Princes went wild as they realised that their team had earned the right to play in Europe's most prestigious club competition.

"It was emotionally very strong," said midfielder Benoit Cauet, who along with his team mates received a standing ovation from the crowd after the final whistle. "It was a nice conclusion to a season which has often been very difficult."

Paris, who relied on a side made up mostly of older players, had a tough season as they never could keep up with the pace set by Monaco. The team from the principality finished with 79 points compared to PSG's 67.

Ironically, the two goals which gave Paris their much-needed win over Strasbourg were scored by two of the veterans who had been blamed for the club's relatively poor form -- Guerin and central defender Paul Le Guen.

"Who scored the goals is not what matters most," said Le Guen. "What really counts is that we've qualified for the European Cup, which was our main goal. People will say what they want but our season hasn't been that bad."

While struggling to follow Monaco in the league, PSG, who won the Cup winners' Cup last year, reached their fifth successive semifinal on the European front and went on to lose their trophy to Barcelona in a hard-fought final.

"If we had reached all our goals, we would have achieved something no French club had even done before," said club president Michel Denisot, who said before the season that he wanted both the league title and victory in the Cup winners' Cup. "I think we can be proud."

Brazilian coach Ricardo, who rarely smiles, looked happy after Saturday's match. "It's wonderful," he said. "Things have not always been easy for us this season but you must give the players credit for never giving up. They fought until the very end and eventually got their reward."
Brazilian playmaker Rai and compatriot Leonardo, arguably the club's strongest assets, have both said they want to stay with PSG next season.
New signings are expected to include promising striker Florian Maurice, who scored two goals to help Lyon crush Marseille 8-0 on Saturday.
"We should have a strong team and we're definitely looking forward to a new challenge," said Ricardo.
